identity.note: Prefix namespace for this product's entity types (governance/identifier-standard.md §2). DECLARED here rather than derived from the repo directory name: a rename would otherwise silently orphan every id already issued, and that surfaces much later as unresolvable references with no obvious cause. Reserved spine prefixes (usr/org/prt/app, billing, messaging) belong to FuzeFront; this product's own types namespace as agent_<type>. Enforced by `gate_identifier.py --namespace`.

a2a.note: CORRECTED 2026-08-23: enabled:false denied a surface that is serving in production. FuzeAgent HOSTS the family's A2A deployment. deploy/helm/a2a-shared/values-prod.yaml — the only valueFile the Argo Application (deploy/argocd/applications/a2a-shared.yaml) lists — carries `a2a.enabled: true` with image tag 51f12786811a, and the `a2a-shared` pod was observed Running 1/1 in the fuzeagent namespace on 2026-08-21 (FuzeInfra cluster-query run 32475207623). It is the ONLY A2A pod in the fleet, by design: the image hardcodes the Agent Card's in-cluster interface URL to a2a-shared.fuzeagent.svc.cluster.local (card_generator.py:29), so per-product pods cannot work and every other product onboards as a `tenants[]` entry here. FuzeAgent is tenant #1 in that list — enabled:true, entryRole agent-orchestrator, external:false — which is exactly what the servingRoles/entryRole below already declared. THE OLD NOTE'S REASONING IS RETAINED AND STILL OPEN: this was left enabled:false pending verification that the card projects schema-valid against the frozen contract (agent-templates/contracts/a2a/v1/schema/manifest-a2a-extension.schema.json). That verification has still not happened, and this change does not perform it — but withholding the flag was never the right way to record an unverified projection, because the flag mirrors the Helm gate and the Helm gate is ON. An unverified card that is being served is a worse thing to hide than to show. a2a-maintainer owns the projection check. WHY THE PREFLIGHT NOW GOES RED, and why that is the point: a2a-maintain's preflight keys off exactly this flag, so enabled:false made the check SKIP and report green about the one A2A server the family actually runs. With enabled:true it runs and fails for want of LITELLM_FUZE_KEY. That red is the true state of an unmaintained live surface, NOT a regression; automated key provisioning is in flight. AUTHORITATIVE CALLER ALLOWLIST is the top-level `providesTo` (22 entries, present), not anything in this block.

mcp.note: REAL, not a scaffold — mcp-servers/fuzeagent-server/ already serves 15+ tools over the hierarchy API. Outstanding: a tools.json declaring `mutates` per tool. Several tools mutate (assign_task, deploy_agent, create_custom_agent, update_task_status, create_organizational_goal, update_goal_progress) and MUST be classified mutates:true; the read tools (list_*, get_*) are mutates:false. Classification is mcp-maintainer's to reconcile.
